original_card.question: Can one measured replay bottleneck be sped up without dropping coverage?
methods: Profile one isolated replay and optimize the measured bottleneck.
Design source-bound reuse with explicit dependency invalidation and negative controls.
original_card.acceptance_gate: Report before/after wall time on the same fixture, retained checks and invalidation behavior.

first_step.inspect: Resolve the current selected review, separate complex/ordinary BIT/admitted BIT/outer budgets, and compare the card against live handoffs before starting. Historical ceilings require exact source/model equivalence.
first_step.scope: Source-binding orientation only; not a scientific replay or all-size proof. Materialize selected inputs if this checkout is sparse.

original_card.first_experiment: Measure one unchanged fixture, preserve check coverage, and test one optimization with invalidation controls.
original_card.bottleneck_link: Faster trustworthy replays increase review throughput and let mechanism candidates be checked sooner.
allowed_variations: Profile one stage or design one source-bound cache boundary.
scope_change_triggers: Skipping coverage or comparing different fixtures to claim speedup.

actual_scope: Defer unused parent-side legacy validation loading in the current task-picker CLI, preserving exact complete outputs, source freshness and historical-route rejection.
scope_change_reason: The first BIT suggestion was not assigned by the donor. Live and recent-account overlap excluded the mathematical tour candidate before research. This uses the current verifier-engineering priority for a distinct original onboarding bottleneck rather than auditing a predecessor.
bottleneck_link: Repeated coordination commands load the same frozen picker twice even when no historical first-step rewrite is needed. Removing the unused load reduces this bounded startup cost; it changes no supplier or scientific replay.
stop_rule: Ship the first measured complete-command improvement after exact conformance and retained rejection checks. Do not expand the optimization.
evidence: The exact-source conformance checker passes all 22 live cards, two historical route shapes and seven source/route rejection controls. The existing 12 routing tests pass. Generated BENCHMARK.json supplies alternating complete-command wall times, every successful command and source hashes. The recorded nine paired batches of ten fresh commands each have medians 104.461 ms before and 99.598 ms after, 4.66% less wall time, with all nine paired decreases positive and zero errors. The ratio is empirical and host-specific.
author: Nick Petalas
ai_assistance: Independent human and formal proof-kernel review are unclaimed.
